concept: Query settings and index filters as plan pinning
summary: Source-anchored research for Query settings and index filters as plan pinning. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Index hints in query settings restrict the planner's available indexes but do not guarantee an index scan; legacy index filters likewise allow a collection scan. Neither mechanism guarantees an exact execution plan. (high confidence)

Before interpreting an index-hiding trial, inspect restrictions that reference the candidate or exclude alternatives. This is a methodological inference: a legacy filter restricted to the hidden index can produce a collection scan even when another visible index could otherwise support the query. (medium confidence)

Tencent recommends restricting only critical queries whose plan drift would cause an incident and reconsidering settings when data distribution changes. MinervaDB similarly presents query settings as a mitigation and recommends removing the setting after a durable indexing correction. (medium confidence)
Legacy index filters last only for the server process. Campbell independently reported rejecting filters in a 2017 production incident because they did not survive restarts. (medium confidence)

MongoDB 8.0 introduced setQuerySettings and deprecated index filters; query settings apply to matching query shapes across the cluster and persist across restarts, while legacy index filters are process-local and disappear at shutdown. (high confidence)

If the indexes named by a legacy index filter do not exist or are hidden, MongoDB documents a collection scan. A hidden index is unavailable to the planner and cannot be selected with cursor.hint(). (high confidence)
If matching query settings contain index hints, MongoDB ignores command-level index hints. A client hint alone therefore cannot prove which index candidates the planner received. (low confidence)

SERVER-60710 reports indexFilterSet remaining false with executionStats verbosity despite an applied filter, tested on 4.4.9 and 5.0.2; the issue lists fix version 6.0.0-rc0. On those historical versions, that flag alone cannot establish that a filter is absent. (low confidence)
MongoDB introduced query settings in 8.0 and deprecated legacy index filters in 8.0. Query settings apply to matching query shapes cluster-wide and persist across restarts. (medium confidence)
MongoDB 8.0 hidden indexes cannot support queries and cannot be selected with cursor.hint(); unhiding a maintained index makes it immediately available again. (low confidence)

Inspect configured query settings with db.aggregate([{ $querySettings: {} }]); remove obsolete settings with removeQuerySettings. Verify applied settings and the actual winning plan with explain. (high confidence)

SERVER-33303 reproduces MongoDB 3.6.2 retaining a legacy filter after dropping its target index but temporarily not applying it; creating another index makes the filter apply again and selects COLLSCAN. The issue lists fix version 4.1.5. This is historical evidence, not a claim that current releases retain the bug. (low confidence)
If all indexes specified by a legacy filter are hidden or absent, the optimizer uses a collection scan. A removal rehearsal must therefore inspect filters, not just index usage. (medium confidence)
For legacy filters, check explain.indexFilterSet. Their shape includes query, sort, projection and collation; predicate literal values do not distinguish matching shapes. (low confidence)

Tencent recommends restricting index choices only for critical queries, testing representative parameters, and revisiting restrictions after data-distribution changes. This is operational guidance, not an execution-plan guarantee. (low confidence)

Campbell reported that a frequent outlier literal caused an index choice unsuitable for most queries sharing its shape. This historical incident motivates testing parameter diversity before applying shape-wide restrictions. (low confidence)
